tokenEstimationSettings.title: Token Estimation
tokenEstimationSettings.activationDescription: Estimation is used only when a provider omits input, output, or total token usage. Provider-reported values always take priority. Estimated values are marked and included in context and aggregate usage.
tokenEstimationSettings.historyDescription: Changes apply only to future estimates. Historical records and provider-reported usage are never recalculated.
tokenEstimationSettings.algorithmDescription: Text is estimated from separate runs of ASCII letters and digits versus other visible characters, then message overhead, tool definitions, and a per-image estimate are added. Tokenizers differ by model, so provider usage remains authoritative.

fields.otherCharsPerToken: CJK and other visible character ratio

defaultConversation.description: Use all settings from this role when creating a standard conversation.

conversationNaming.triggerTokenDescription: Create an automatic naming functional conversation when the latest complete request context reaches this value. The default is 20K; the configured token estimator is used when the provider reports no usage.
conversationNaming.cacheHitOptimizationDescription: Reuse the model, generation settings, and conversation prefix from the real request that triggered naming, then append the automatic naming task.
conversationNaming.cacheHitOptimizationSettingsNote: Model, reasoning, temperature, Top P, and maximum output length all follow the latest real request that triggered naming.
conversationNaming.cacheHitOptimizationBoundaryNote: Naming material accumulates from the conversation start through the threshold, then rounds forward to the next complete legal message group. Tool calls are never separated from their tool results. No task is created without a real request snapshot and a legal boundary.

memoryCompression.blockingDescription: When enabled, the current conversation waits for compaction to finish after reaching the threshold. When disabled, compaction runs asynchronously in the background.
memoryCompression.cacheHitOptimizationDescription: Reuse the actual conversation model and request prefix that triggered compression, then append only the memory-compression task to improve the chance of an upstream context-cache hit and reduce repeated input costs.
memoryCompression.cacheHitOptimizationSettingsNote: The model and reasoning settings follow the triggering request; temperature, Top P, and maximum output length still use the settings on this page.
memoryCompression.cacheHitOptimizationBoundaryNote: Cache hits depend on the provider and are not guaranteed. If the real request snapshot is missing or the compression boundary cannot be located precisely, compression fails explicitly and does not switch to a dedicated model.

longTermMemoryManagement.projectTriggerTokenDescription: Create a project memory management functional conversation when complete valid message groups added since the last successful run reach this value. Default: 50K. Tool calls are never separated from their results.
longTermMemoryManagement.globalTriggerTokenDescription: Create a global memory management functional conversation when complete valid message groups added since the last successful run reach this value. Default: 100K. Tool calls are never separated from their results.
longTermMemoryManagement.blockingDescription: When enabled, the current conversation waits for long-term memory management to finish after reaching the threshold. When disabled, it runs asynchronously in the background.
longTermMemoryManagement.cacheHitOptimizationDescription: Reuse the real request model, generation settings, and complete effective conversation prefix that triggered the task, then append the long-term memory management task.
longTermMemoryManagement.cacheHitOptimizationSettingsNote: Model, reasoning, temperature, Top P, and maximum output length all follow the latest real request that triggered the task.
longTermMemoryManagement.cacheHitOptimizationBoundaryNote: Each task reads the current complete effective history. The incremental boundary advances only after manage_memory succeeds. Messages added during an asynchronous run are handled by the next task.
